body:
Hi @DefaultXYZ,

Thanks for the detailed bug report and minimal reproduction project — I’ve reviewed the issue and confirmed it on my end as well.

✅ Confirmed on:
Godot 4.4.1.mono and 4.5.beta3.mono

Windows 11

Manually created C# plugin (with plugin.cfg and .cs script) is not detected, despite valid structure and Tool attribute.

🔍 Likely cause:
The Godot plugin loader expects the script entry in plugin.cfg to be a GDScript path, and does not currently resolve .cs paths correctly, unless the plugin is created via the built-in editor tooling.

It also appears that C# plugin scripts are not initialized at the time plugin.cfg is parsed, resulting in the warning:
```Plugin config at "res://addons/MyPlugin/plugin.cfg" is missing the following keys...```

🔧 Workaround:
For now, you can:

Open the Godot Editor.

Go to Project > Project Settings > Plugins tab.

Click “Create” to generate the plugin via the editor UI — this correctly sets up a working plugin.cfg and script binding.

Then replace the generated .gd file with your .cs plugin, making sure:

The C# script inherits EditorPlugin

It is marked with [Tool]

The plugin.cfg script field points to:
```script = "res://addons/YourPlugin/YourPlugin.cs"```

After that, restart the editor and the plugin should appear in the Plugins tab.

💡 Suggestion for improvement:
Godot could add explicit support for .cs scripts in plugin.cfg, or at the very least give a clearer warning or fallback behavior when detecting .cs-based EditorPlugins.

Let me know if you'd like help generating a working C# plugin template — happy to help!

Best regards,

@Storm-Dev6 C# is supported in the `plugin.cfg` script field, just like any other scripting language. You just need to make sure the C# project is built before enabling the plugin, but if this was the issue you'd be getting a different error. The error the user is getting is complaining specifically about parsing the `plugin.cfg` so it doesn't seem related to the scripting language.

@DefaultXYZ I downloaded the MRP you provided and the `plugin.cfg` file for the C# plugin seems to be saved with UTF8-with-BOM encoding. Re-saving it without BOM seems to make it appear in the Plugins list.

Thank you for looking into it, highly appreciated!

I thought it could be something with encoding, but didn't pay enough patience with it😅
